items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Because Duke Ellyn was playing nice sweet stuff and things and they kidded him.

ctx.x: But one thing I will say, I don't know, the Chicago people when I first got there, they liked it more blues numbers like. Because Duke Ellyn was playing nice sweet stuff and things and they kidded him. But when Louis went there with all that jumping and clowning and all kind of felt like me, you know, and the other people went for that, crazy about that. But later on they got to going for that nice music, you know. Later on, yeah, they got to going for that classic stuff. Later on.
Do they have more shows in Chicago than here, or more here?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: That was this B-guard, where he was Duke.

ctx.x: Pils? Well, it wasn't much to Pils. Wasn't much to Pils. Now I'll tell you a fella, I don't know about, I didn't hear him here, but he fun, you have to tell me, but he played a lot of clarinet. That was this B-guard, where he was Duke. Now I'll tell you who I played with here before he left a little bit, Sidney Bischie, but not much, because he left as soon as I come in the hall and he left. He left right after Lewis, you tell me.
He must have left before Lewis, because you played with Lewis down here.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: He was with Duke Elton. Or Duke Armstrong or somebody.

ctx.x: What about down here, Punch? When you got down? No.

I'm going to tell him something first. Red Allen named his daddy. Henry Allen. That's right. All right. Now, as you talk about the old man and the young one. The young one. The young one? Yeah. No. But I tell you what I did. I taught him a whole lot. You taught Red Allen a lot? I taught Red Allen a whole lot. I know Red Allen very well. Well, he's a younger kid now. I mean, I believe he looked old, but he's a young fella. Taught Red Allen. All right. That's fine. There was a kid in him at the Garrick Bar in…
Punch, in 1919, when you first got here, what did the brass bands play like? Were they strictly music? Were they here?
